chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Upon the person who is performing Qiran (or Tamattu') [the Sa'ri], it is obligatory to shave his head completely and not merely trim [the hair]; indeed, trimming is [sufficient] for the one who performed the Hajj of Islam."

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Trimming or cutting the hair short (not shaving)
key_terms.الصَّرُورَةِ: The state of being bound by the Hajj rites (Sa'ri), often referring to Qiran or Tamattu'
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The Hajj of Islam (the first obligatory Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shaving and trimming hair after Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the obligatory head shaving (halq) required for the Sa'ri state in Qiran or Tamattu' Hajj and the lesser trimming (qasr) sufficient for the Hajjat al-Islam. This ruling highlights the specific ritual obligations tied to the type of Hajj performed, emphasizing the completeness of the sacrifice in the Sa'ri state. The hadith serves as a key legal precedent in Shia fiqh for differentiating between the degrees of ritual completion based on the pilgrim's initial intention.
